title: GST Compliance — from GST data to a fast read model
takeaway: Returns status is read from a projection kept fresh by domain events, not derived on request.
steps: Invoices, purchase registers and portal data enter as GST data.
They land in four stores: Books, IMS, GSTR-2B and the GSTR-1 / GSTR-3B filings.
M9 reconciliation matches Books, IMS and GSTR-2B and classifies each document as EXACT, MISMATCH, MISSING_IN_2B, MISSING_IN_BOOKS or DRIFT; the result is delivered over SSE.
GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B writers emit source-changed domain events that update a precomputed returns status projection.
The returns read model serves queries directly: 3,000ms+ before, sub-15ms at peak load after.

title: Dynamic QR — two concurrent scans, one unit left
takeaway: Under concurrent scans, the lock makes the decrement atomic: one unit, one redemption.
steps: Two scans arrive at the same moment for a campaign line with one unit of inventory.
Both pass pre-validation, which runs before the database is touched.
Both see inventory available, then contend for the Redis lock; one holds it, the other waits.
The holder redeems atomically: inventory 1 → 0, scan history recorded, response returned.
The waiting scan acquires the lock, re-reads inventory at 0 and is rejected — no double redemption.
Live inventory stats stream to the dashboard over SSE.

title: BARA — retrieval as a decision
takeaway: Retrieval is a decision made by deterministic gates, not a reflex on every message.
steps: Four memory tiers: research memory, conversational state, semantic profile and episodic memory.
Each message is classified for intent, conversation type and behavioural shift, then threaded to a topic.
The policy's 41 deterministic gates decide whether to retrieve and from which tiers.
An acknowledgement-style message retrieves nothing and goes straight to the LLM.
A message that refers back to earlier decisions opens only the research and episodic tiers.
Selected context is passed to the multi-provider LLM client, which produces the response.

title: Antigravity — review without write access to main
takeaway: Every pass runs inside a disposable worktree; the main branch is never touched.
steps: A pull request labelled review-requested is picked up by the daemon.
It is checked out into an isolated git worktree at the PR's head commit.
Five passes run inside the worktree: CodeGraph impact analysis, tenant-isolation AST check, TypeScript, ESLint and dependency-cruiser.
The evidence gate drops findings without a diff-anchored line.
The remaining findings are posted as a GitHub review with REQUEST_CHANGES or APPROVE.
The worktree is removed. The main branch is untouched.

title: ACFS — every finding points back to one file
takeaway: The report carries the SHA-256 of the original artifact, so its findings stay tied to the exact file they describe.
steps: An artifact arrives and the SHA-256 hash of the original is computed before any analysis.
Independent analyses read the same file: a fine-tuned ViT / DeiT classifier, error level analysis and EXIF anomaly checks.
The classifier's attention is rendered as a Grad-CAM heatmap.
Each finding flows into one PDF forensic report.
The digest computed at intake is printed in the report as the SHA-256 of the original.

title: DHVVS — anchor a hash, and any edit shows
takeaway: The chain stores a hash of the verified visit, so a retroactive edit to the database record no longer matches it.
steps: An NFC tag or encrypted QR proves presence at the patient's door; GPS geofencing adds a second assertion.
The visit payload is ECDSA-signed on the health worker's device before any network call.
The NestJS API verifies the signature and persists the record in PostgreSQL.
A BullMQ job anchors a hash of the verified record on an EVM Layer-2.
If a field is edited afterwards, the record's hash no longer matches the anchored hash.
Restoring the original record makes the hashes match again.

title: Systems film — four systems, one architecture
takeaway: Concurrency control, an asynchronous document pipeline, reconciliation with a read model, and gated retrieval beside isolated review — each a part of one architecture.
steps: Dynamic QR platform: two scans reach the same campaign line with one unit left. A Redis lock makes the decrement atomic; one scan redeems, the other re-reads 0 and is rejected.

GST platform: an invoice passes the invoice guard, lands in GCS and goes to LlamaIndex Cloud; the signed webhook is verified, the result is mapped and handed to the core service through BullMQ, and structured data reaches the ledger in PostgreSQL.
M9 reconciliation matches purchase books against IMS and GSTR-2B and classifies each document as EXACT, MISMATCH, MISSING_IN_2B, MISSING_IN_BOOKS or DRIFT; the result is delivered over SSE.
Return status was assembled on every read (3,000ms+); GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B writers now keep a precomputed projection fresh, and the read takes under 15ms at peak load.
BARA classifies each message first; 41 deterministic gates decide whether to retrieve. An acknowledgement retrieves nothing; a message that refers back opens only the research and episodic tiers.
Antigravity reviews a pull request in a temporary worktree; a finding without a diff line is dropped, the worktree is removed, and the main branch is never touched.

The systems resolve into the architecture on the homepage: Redis, BullMQ and workers, the AI pipeline, PostgreSQL, the NestJS API, SSE and pgvector memory. That topology contracts into the K mark from the site header, followed by the name, the role and the site headline.
